# Session Start — Ready Before You Touch Code

_Applies when: the first move of every session, before any implementation is dispatched._

Every chat opens the same way. Part of the opening is **mechanical** — the harness does it,
no action needed. The rest is **discipline** — the agent must actively do it, or the session
starts blind. Knowing which is which stops prose from looking more binding than it is.

## Mechanical — the harness already did this (nothing to do)

- **Config is fresh.** On Claude, the SessionStart hook ran `agent-core sync --scope global`;
  OpenCode ships the same rules via its bundle. Rules/skills/agents/MCP are current this session.
- **Session defaults are seeded, not forced** — model, effort, ultracode, workflows — see
  `06-model-effort` (seed-only per ADR-0013; never re-negotiate them inline).
- **Delegate-only is enforced.** The orchestrator's `Edit`/`Write` is denied (Claude guard hook
  by `agent_id`; OpenCode `build.permission.edit=deny`) — see `25-orchestration`.
- **(OpenCode) memory + version scaffold** ran on `session.created`.

## Discipline — do this before dispatching work (Definition of Ready)

1. **Orient.** Read `project-standards.md` and the board (`.scrum/`, see `20-workflow`) — know the
   stack versions and where the work sits before planning.
2. **Load memory.** Read the project memory index (`memory/MEMORY.md`) so prior decisions,
   gotchas and constraints carry over — see `23-memory-discipline`.
3. **Pick the effort tier** — Bugfix / Lite / Full (`20-workflow`). Ceremony, not reasoning effort;
   effort stays maximal (`06-model-effort`).
4. **One decision first.** Surface the single deciding question and get an answer **before** any
   fan-out or architecture move (`25-orchestration`, plan-first).
5. **Branch before edits.** For implementation work, create a `feat/…` or `fix/…` branch up front
   (a Bash step the orchestrator does itself, not an edit) — never work on `main` (`20-workflow`).
   Pure Q&A / reading needs no branch.

A session that skipped 1–2 is not ready — a fresh chat has no memory of its own past. Ready means:
oriented, memory loaded, tier chosen, deciding question asked, branch in place.
